question.prompt: A set \(S\) is constructed as follows. To begin, \(S=\{0,10\}.\) Repeatedly, as long as possible, if \(x\) is an integer root of some polynomial \(a_nx^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}\) \(+\cdots+a_1x+a_0\) for some \(n\ge1,\) all of whose coefficients \(a_i\) are elements of \(S,\) then \(x\) is put into \(S.\) When no more elements can be added to \(S,\) how many elements does \(S\) have?

solutions.title: Construct roots and prove the set stops
solutions.explanation:
The useful restriction is divisibility: after removing any factor that is a power of the variable, a nonzero integer root must divide the remaining constant term. This suggests examining the signed divisors of 10.

First, we can obtain all the elements of
\[
T=\{0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm5,\pm10\}.
\]
Starting from \(\{0,10\}\), use the following polynomials in order. Each row uses only coefficients already available, and the indicated new element is a root.
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
\text{new element}&\text{polynomial}\\ \hline
-1&10t+10\\
1&10-t-t^2-\cdots-t^{10}\\
-10&t+10\\
2&t^3+t-10\\
-2&t+2\\
5&2t-10\\
-5&2t+10
\end{array}
\]
For the two nonlinear polynomials, substitution gives \(10-10=0\) at \(t=1\) and \(8+2-10=0\) at \(t=2\). The other root checks follow directly from their linear equations.

Now we must prove that nothing outside \(T\) can appear. Take any nonzero polynomial \(P(t)\) whose coefficients belong to \(T\). Factor out its lowest occurring power of \(t\):
\[
P(t)=t^jQ(t),\qquad Q(0)=c\ne0.
\]
The number \(c\) is a nonzero coefficient of \(P\), so it belongs to \(T\). Write \(Q(t)=c+tR(t)\), where \(R\) has integer coefficients. If a nonzero integer \(r\) is a root of \(P\), then \(Q(r)=0\), giving
\[
c=-rR(r).
\]
Thus \(r\mid c\). Every possible nonzero \(c\) divides 10, so \(r\mid10\). Hence \(r\) is already in \(T\); the root 0 is also already there.

This proves that the rule cannot produce an element outside \(T\). Since the constructions produce every member of \(T\), the final set is exactly \(T\), with
\[
1+2\cdot4=\boxed{9}
\]
elements. The answer is D.
